headline: Deadlocked adds PAL drawing, movement and lookup routines in matching C
summary: Deadlocked’s PAL version gains matching C for drawing wrappers, point transforms, smoothing, object access and table lookups. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. These PAL additions do not move the separate NTSC-U v1.00 progress figure, which remains at 6.07% of code by size, unchanged from the previous day, with 4,475 of 18,085 functions matched.
highlights: PAL batches include 30 functions in #54, seventeen fixed-size hash lookups in #72 and 22 game functions in #75. Drawing and point-transform routines also land (#57, #60).
Contributors can extract a disc image stored outside the checkout by supplying its path, without copying or linking it into the project (#56).
Draft #71 proposes 45 NTSC-U helper matches but still needs PAL mapping before merge. Its author lacks PAL retail inputs locally.
PAL proposals #55, #77, #78 and #79 remain unmerged. Issue #73 shares reconstruction findings and unmatched drafts, not a claim that every generated code range is a decompiled function.
